q: In a parallel combination of capacitors, all the capacitors have the same _____.
e: In a parallel combination of capacitors, all the capacitors have the same potential difference. charge is not potential difference, and resistance is not potential difference either. Parallel capacitors share voltage, charges add, and equivalent C is the sum. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.

q: In a parallel combination, the total charge Q is the _____ of the individual charges.
e: In a parallel combination, the total charge Q is the sum of the individual charges. Put product or reciprocal in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add.

q: The equivalent capacitance C of capacitors in parallel is C = _____.
e: The equivalent capacitance C of capacitors in parallel is C = C1 + C2 + C3. C1 C2 / (C1 + C2) is not C1 + C2 + C3, and 1/C1 + 1/C2 is not C1 + C2 + C3 either. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add.

q: The equivalent capacitance of capacitors connected in parallel is the _____ of the capacitances of the individual capacitors.
e: The equivalent capacitance of capacitors connected in parallel is the sum of the capacitances of the individual capacitors. reciprocal sum is not sum, and product is not sum either. Parallel capacitors share voltage, charges add, and equivalent C is the sum.

q: The equivalent capacitance of the parallel combination of n identical capacitors, each of capacitance $C_1$, is C = _____.
e: The equivalent capacitance of the parallel combination of n identical capacitors, each of capacitance C1, is C = nC1. Put C1/n or C1^n in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Parallel capacitors share voltage, charges add, and equivalent C is the sum. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.

q: In a series combination of capacitors, each capacitor has the same _____.
e: In a series combination of capacitors, each capacitor has the same charge. Put potential difference or energy in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates.

q: In a series combination, the capacitors have different _____.
e: In a series combination, the capacitors have different potential differences. Put dielectrics or charges in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Series capacitors share charge, voltages add, and equivalent C is smaller than the smallest.

q: The total potential difference V of a series capacitor combination is the _____ of individual potential differences.
e: The total potential difference V of a series capacitor combination is the reciprocal of individual potential differences. Put sum or product in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Potential difference is the electrical push between two points; no push, no current. In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add.

q: For capacitors in series, the reciprocal of the equivalent capacitance is the sum of the _____ of their individual capacitances.
e: For capacitors in series, the reciprocal of the equivalent capacitance is the sum of the reciprocals of their individual capacitances. Put squares or cubes in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add.

q: The equivalent capacitance C of the series combination of n identical capacitors, each of capacitance $C_1$, is C = _____.
e: The equivalent capacitance C of the series combination of n identical capacitors, each of capacitance C1, is C = C1/n. Put nC1 or n/C1 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add.

q: In a parallel circuit diagram, the plates of the capacitors connected together at the point A have _____ charges.
e: In a parallel circuit diagram, the plates of the capacitors connected together at the point A have neutral charges. Put positive or negative in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add. Parallel capacitors share voltage, charges add, and equivalent C is the sum.

q: In a series circuit diagram, the negatively charged plate of one capacitor is connected to the _____ charged plate of the other.
e: In a series circuit diagram, the negatively charged plate of one capacitor is connected to the positively charged plate of the other. negatively is not positively, and neutrally is not positively either. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.

q: There are two types of combination namely; (i) parallel and (ii) _____.
e: There are two types of combination namely; (i) parallel and (ii) series. Put circular or diagonal in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add.
